faq.q: Why is hot water taken from the top of the tank?
faq.a: Because the hottest water floats to the top. Drawing from there gives you the hottest water first, even if the bottom of the tank is still cool.
asks: How does a hot water tank work?

faq.q: What heats the water in a cylinder?
faq.a: A coil of copper pipe carrying hot water from the boiler, or an electric immersion heater, or sometimes both. They heat the stored water without mixing with it.
asks: What is the coil in a hot water tank?

faq.q: Why does cold water go in at the bottom?
faq.a: Cold water is denser, so it stays at the bottom and gently pushes the hot layer up. Putting it in at the top would mix and cool everything.
asks: Where does the cold water enter the cylinder?

faq.q: Why is stored hot water kept at about 60 °C?
faq.a: Keeping it at about 60 degrees kills Legionella bacteria, which can grow in lukewarm water and cause a serious lung illness.
asks: Why is my hot water tank set so hot?

faq.q: Why is the cylinder wrapped in foam?
faq.a: The foam insulation stops heat escaping into the cupboard, so the water stays hot for hours and less energy is wasted.
asks: Why insulate a hot water tank?

facts: Stored hot water is usually kept at about 60 °C to stop Legionella bacteria growing.
In a hot-water cylinder, hot water floats above cooler water, so it is drawn off from the top.
